claim: Humans solve unfamiliar abstract grid puzzles at high rates: 76.2% (training) and 64.2% (public eval) in 1,729 online people; ConceptARC humans 91%; 790 of 800 ARC tasks solved by at least one person.
agent_test: Run our agent on H-ARC items at equal tokens and compare to the 64% human mean.

claim: LLMs without search or training fall far below humans on novel abstract reasoning (GPT-4 about 25% on ConceptARC vs 91% humans; per-concept 0.03 to 0.33; ARC open QA 0.119).
agent_test: Same items, plain arm vs scaffold arm at equal tokens.

claim: Part of the gap is representation: object representation raises GPT-4 on simple ARC tasks from 13/50 to 23/50, and code execution closes the human-GPT-4 gap on letter-string tasks. Gap search: the best representation depends on model type (pixel canvas for vision models, d07), so no single rewrite step is robust.
agent_test: Test a grid-to-object rewrite step vs raw grid at equal tokens.

claim: Counterfactual variants (changed alphabet, base, orientation) break LLM performance while human accuracy stays flat; early claims of emergent analogy in GPT-3 were not robust.
agent_test: Run original and counterfactual versions of each task; treat a large drop as a memorisation flag.

claim: The size of the counterfactual gap is contested: Webb 2024 finds GPT-4 with code matches humans; Lewis and Mitchell find a gap; GPT-3 per-task results differ across Webb, Hodel and West, and Lewis and Mitchell.
agent_test: Replicate with one fixed prompt across tasks and models.

claim: Test-time training lifts ARC sharply: 17.5% to 45.0% pass@2 on 80 tasks, 53.0% with an 8B model, 61.9% with a program-synthesis ensemble.
agent_test: Proxy only: iterative refine harness at equal tokens.

claim: Induction (write a program) and transduction (answer directly) solve different ARC tasks; each alone about 40%, ensemble 56.75%.
agent_test: Arm: program-first with direct-answer fallback vs either alone.

claim: Hypothesis then program verification helps GPT-4 on a 100-problem ARC subset: 17% direct, 23% programs, 30% with summarised hypotheses; language-only 19%.
agent_test: Replicate on our model against an equal-token direct baseline.

claim: Reasoning models collapse on harder Raven variants: o3-mini 86.6% to 17.0% (chance 12.5%) while using more reasoning tokens; neuro-symbolic 98.6% to 88.0%. Gap search: two more papers (Gema 2025, NeuroCognition 2026) show longer reasoning lowering accuracy on other tasks, but not the Raven numbers themselves.
agent_test: Check whether longer reasoning helps or hurts on novel items; test a stop rule.

claim: ARC-AGI-1 is near saturated for frontier systems but ARC-AGI-2 stays low in 2025 (o3-medium 53% vs 3%); ARC Prize 2025 top 24.03%; a refinement harness lifts Gemini 3 Pro from 31% to 54% at about 38x cost.
agent_test: Report accuracy per token with and without the refinement loop.

claim: Working-memory training does not reliably raise Gf: Jaeggi 2008 (N=70, d=0.65 vs 0.25) was not replicated; meta-analysis g=0.05 for nonverbal ability vs treated controls.
agent_test: Not applicable to a frozen model.

claim: Matrix-reasoning success in humans relates to holding and comparing items: eye-movement toggling rate vs score r=-0.68 (N=34).
agent_test: Limit items held per step and measure accuracy.

claim: LLM general-factor score rises with parameter count with diminishing returns (r=0.54) and one factor explains 65.6% of variance across tests.
agent_test: Check scaffold gain against model size.

claim: Flynn effect is about 2.31 IQ points per decade (285 studies), no fading; education adds roughly 1 to 5 points per year.
agent_test: Background only.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Gf peaks around age 27 and declines while Gc keeps rising (Horn and Cattell 1967); known only secondhand here. Gap search: still not read; publisher text unavailable (d15).
agent_test: Background; primary papers not read.

claim: Small purpose-built models do well on ARC-AGI-1: TRM 7M parameters 45% (about 8% on ARC-AGI-2); CompressARC 76K parameters about 20%.
agent_test: No direct test; shows novelty skill is not tied to scale.

claim: Multi-rule and progression items are hardest for GPT-3 relative to humans (progression odds ratio 0.07 vs 0.41).
agent_test: Tag items by rule count and check where the agent drops.

claim: Longer reasoning can lower accuracy: Zebra constraint puzzles and distractor counting show inverse scaling, stronger when the model picks its own length (R1 70% to 30% at 5 distractors); text Raven items with 8 options improve when reasoning is turned off (p=.021).
agent_test: Plot accuracy against reasoning tokens on our own novel and familiar items; test a hard cap.

claim: Human difficulty does not predict model difficulty on ARC: fine-tuned models beat humans on the hardest 20% of tasks and trail them on the easiest 20%.
agent_test: Build the S0 novelty sort from pilot model attempts, not from human novelty ratings; check the sort against outcomes.

claim: Contamination of ARC by public data is suspected by the benchmark owners but not quantified; the only fresh-task evidence is the ARC-AGI-1 to ARC-AGI-2 drop and one anecdote of unprompted ARC color mappings. Memorisation can be measured by perturbation consistency (Knights and Knaves study).
agent_test: Add perturbed copies of test items and report the share solved only in the original form.

claim: Program induction checked against the demonstration pairs, with search and refinement, lifts models far above one-shot: open models 1-2% to 14-26% with search and 36-45% after learning from traces; best 52% on ARC-AGI-1 public test; prompt-level harness on Gemini 3 Pro 31% to 54% on ARC-AGI-2 at 38x cost.
agent_test: Run hypothesis-program-check against plain chain-of-thought at equal tokens and at 10x tokens.

claim: LLM working-memory limits do not mirror human item-count limits: failures are in using or carrying state (latent state drift, ignoring supplied history) and in run-to-run consistency, not in holding a fixed number of items. Human-style n-back readings are disputed.
agent_test: Write every held item to notes; run each item twice and flag disagreement.

claim: Human Raven and ARC norms do not transfer to LLM scoring: human image norm (0.814) cannot be applied to text matrices (humans 0.43 on text pilot, N=9), and format changes (multiple choice vs free answer) swing model scores in opposite directions.
agent_test: Always run a matched human or baseline arm in the same format; never quote a human norm from a different format.
